abstract: The incidence of testicular cancer has increased markedly in most developed countries, although the reasons for this are unclear. In this study, 253 patients with testicular cancer diagnosed younger than 25 years from 1968-1999 were identified from the Northern Region Young Persons' Malignant Disease Registry. The age-standardized incidence rate increased from 0.93 in 1968-1978 to 1.60 per 100,000 in 1990-1999. The increase in incidence was confined to those patients >15 years old, with the rate in younger children remaining very low. The 5-year survival increased significantly from 46% (95% confidence interval [CI] 33% to 58%) to 92% (95% CI 85% to 96%) during 1968-1999 and was significantly higher for seminoma than nonseminoma, 91% (95% CI 78% to 96%) and 77% (95% CI 70% to 82%), respectively. Although increased surveillance and public health campaigns designed to raise awareness of the disease and the advantages of self-examination should continue, further research is required into the etiology of this relatively common cancer among young males.
abstract_ja: 精巣がんは多くの先進国で著しく増加しているが、その理由は不明である。本研究では、Northern Region Young Person's Malignant Disease Registryから、1968年から1999年に25歳未満で診断された精巣がん患者253例を同定した。年齢調整罹患率は1968〜1978年の10万人あたり0.93から1990〜1999年の1.60へ増加した。増加は15歳を超える患者に限られ、若年小児の発生率は非常に低いままであった。5年生存率は1968〜1999年の間に46%(95%信頼区間33%〜58%)から92%(95%信頼区間85%〜96%)へ有意に向上した。セミノーマの生存率は非セミノーマより有意に高かった(それぞれ91%(95%信頼区間78%〜96%)と77%(95%信頼区間70%〜82%))。検診・監視の強化や自己検査の利点に関する啓発などの公衆衛生活動は継続すべきであるが、この比較的一般的ながんの若年男性における病因についてはさらなる研究が必要である。
